title: VPC Operator Safe Mode and Offline Validation Checklist for Private Deploys
creator: Aisha Gopal
description: Define a minimal, operator-invokable 'Safe Mode' state and an offline validation checklist to ensure Private/VPC deployments can be brought to a predictable, repairable state during networking maintenance, restricted egress windows, or full air-gapped operation. This ticket captures the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout/readiness checklist necessary for Private customers to perform upgrades and emergency operations with limited or no egress while preserving ability to rollback, validate artifacts, and maintain SLOs where possible.
background: Customers with isolated VPCs frequently need a deterministic maintenance path for upgrades and emergency fixes where outbound egress is restricted or disabled. Existing acceptance artifacts focus on image mirroring and offline bootstrap; we need an operator-level Safe Mode that: (1) quiesces non-essential components, (2) prevents automatic outbound pulls (images, OS updates), (3) switches to local mirrors and pre-seeded artifacts, and (4) extends health-check windows to reduce false-positive failures during network interruptions.
scope: In scope: product-level requirements for a Safe Mode feature exposed in the Private control plane and operator CLI; the offline validation checklist required prior to, during, and after upgrades; automated preflight checks and a set of deterministic tests to emulate partial and full egress loss. Also includes runbook content and console indicators for Safe Mode state. Out of scope: changes to customer firewall appliances, partner-managed mirrors, and bringing new mirror/proxy infrastructure online (those are customer responsibilities).
out_of_scope: On-prem hardware provisioning, third-party mirror SLAs, bespoke customer automation beyond templated hooks, and migration tooling for cloud-provider-specific firewall rules.
acceptance_criteria: Console and CLI: operator can toggle Safe Mode for a given Private deployment and view its state in the Console within 5s.
Egress controls: when Safe Mode is active, runtime will disable non-essential outbound artifact pulls and enforce image sources to local mirror or signed images present in pre-seeded registries.
Upgrade gating: automatic upgrade pipelines are paused; canaries require explicit operator confirmation when Safe Mode is active.
Artifact verification: runtime validates image and package signatures against customer-provided signing keys (or cached verification metadata) before allowing load.
Preflight checks: a set of preflight checks runs and reports pass/fail; a non-blocking warning is produced for optional checks and blocks on critical checks like missing signed artifacts.
Rollback safety: if a canary fails in Safe Mode, system triggers an automated rollback path to the last known good image without requiring egress to external registries.
Telemetry: Console surfaces Safe Mode metrics (time entered, egress-blocked count, artifacts resolved from mirror) and emits events to audit logs with operator identity.

Test harness: customers or Redwood SEs can execute a standard offline simulation that validates Safe Mode behaviors (simulate DNS/proxy drop, mirror unreachable, mirror-only pulls) and returns a reproducible validation report.
Runbook: a minimal runbook is available that includes step-by-step instructions for entering/exiting Safe Mode, performing upgrades, and validation checks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement API/CLI + Console indicator and preflight checks behind a feature flag in private deployments (internal dogfood). Phase 2: publish runbook and test harness; invite three early customers for guided validation and collect feedback. Phase 3: GA with default Safe Mode checkbox in upgrade workflows and developer docs updated. Feature flag to be removed after two successful customer validations and one internal incident dry-run.
test_plan: Preflight pass/fail matrix run in lab: verify signed-image-only mode, local-mirror pull success, and image fallback behavior.
Simulated partial egress loss: block specific domains and verify operation degradation matches expectations (graceful pause, extended probes).
Simulated full egress loss: confirm restart/upgrade flows complete from pre-seeded artifacts and that rollback path works without external fetch.
Chaos validation: runchaos test for network partition and observe Safe Mode health windows to ensure no false-positive escalations for 30 minutes.
Audit/telemetry validation: verify events are emitted to audit-log, and metrics show accurate counts for blocked egress and mirror pulls.
decisions: Safe Mode will be an explicit operator action (no automatic trigger) for initial GA to reduce accidental enactment risk.
Artifact signature validation will support customer-passed public keys and local cached verification metadata; full KMS integration deferred to a follow-up ticket.
Upgrade pipelines will respect Safe Mode and require explicit operator confirmation for canary promotions when active.
open_questions: Should Safe Mode support scheduled maintenance windows (auto-enter/exit)? Tradeoffs: convenience vs accidental entry.
What is the minimum set of runtime services considered 'essential' (control plane vs agent features) to keep online during Safe Mode?
Do we provide a lightweight on-box artifact verifier to avoid control plane dependency in fully air-gapped environments?
